a write is a read-modify-write — the engine must hold the page before it can change it
and reaching the right leaf page means walking the index, which is more reads still
GetPage@LSN — the leaf page this row lands on is cached nowhere local
the page, at or above that LSN
skipped entirely if the row lands on a freshly allocated page — nothing to read
change the page in memory, generate the log records,
assign the LSNs — the primary is the sequencer
no data page is written to durable storage here, or ever, by this node
log write, over RBIO
the primary's only durable write · WRITELOG
hardened
COMMIT
DURABLE AT STEP 6, COMMITTED AT STEP 7 — EVERYTHING BELOW IS ASYNCHRONOUS
three independent branches — order holds down a branch, but never across them
the application already has its answer
and is waiting on none of this
to the page servers
only the blocks touching this slice
redo every record it is sent —
this tier is the authoritative copy
write the pages down, in the background
its own cadence — this transaction does not trigger it
to the replicas
the whole stream, unfiltered
redo only pages it already
holds cached; skip the rest
meanwhile, a different session — the chart view — reads, routed here
it touched a page this replica skipped — GetPage@LSN,
at the LSN this replica has applied, not the latest
to long-term log
destage the log to long-term storage
also a background cadence of its own
What the line proves
Durability belongs to the log service, not to a replica.
Commit latency therefore does not grow as replicas are
added — in an availability group, every secondary hardens.
Nothing below the line is on this commit's path: it is
bookkeeping, or it belongs to another session.
If it rolls back instead
Nothing undoes back UP this diagram. The abort is simply
more log, travelling steps 8 and 11 like any other record.
Accelerated Database Recovery marks it aborted and frees
the locks at once; versions revert later, out of the PVS.
Rollback is therefore constant time, whatever it touched.
Where a request is parked, by step
PAGEIOLATCH_*
steps 2–3 and 14 — a remote page read
WRITELOG
step 5 — hardening in the log service
RBIO_RG_*
step 4 — the primary throttled by a lagging consumer
The wait tells you which tier the request is waiting on, which
is the practical use of knowing this sequence at all.
